### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in ATTACHMENT_OBJECT; a string literal in computeParentVisibilityFilter; a string literal in installAttachmentReadVisibility))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via installAttachmentReadVisibility (symbol, a top-level function), canReadObject (literal, a string literal in AttachmentReadAdmissionSource), sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in ATTACHMENT_OBJECT; a string literal in computeParentVisibilityFilter; a string literal in installAttachmentReadVisibility))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in ATTACHMENT_OBJECT; a string literal in computeParentVisibilityFilter; a string literal in installAttachmentReadVisibility))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in ATTACHMENT_OBJECT; a string literal in computeParentVisibilityFilter; a string literal in installAttachmentReadVisibility))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f1498cfb124185c6c7e007ce96c0d6426ae8f426` — the merge of head `39991560cdc4a0938c1a9a7541497291237ab2ef` into base `4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f1498cfb124185c6c7e007ce96c0d6426ae8f426 && git checkout f1498cfb124185c6c7e007ce96c0d6426ae8f426
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597 39991560cdc4a0938c1a9a7541497291237ab2ef && git checkout -B drift-repro 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597 && git merge --no-ff 39991560cdc4a0938c1a9a7541497291237ab2ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4fe8b3def02ff9803a52c2fb8b97778d5bf45597` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a664ab3e55af6ee93a350ae608a01c1e67703173`
Local-runs: none

PR #23767 for card #23732 (ADR-0139 row E7, the attachment gate only). Inputs: the card's body and its three comments (triage 6204060336, the claim 6204165226, the dev report 6205457291); the PR's body, its 7-file list and its net diff against `main` at `a869ea6362` (the merge base of the head and that sha is `a869ea6362` itself, and the diff's stat equals the file list); the check-runs on the head; ADR-0139 (D1 to D5 with D5's numbered classes, the plan's row E7, the consumer table, Consequences, O2 and O3) and ADR-0112; #22788 with its amended pin set 6197472558; E5's PR #23693 (`69351e985a`), its body, its changeset and its contract record 6196593905; PR #23663 (`94924e01c1`); PR #22513 (`ce3d0ad419`), its body, its changesets and its contract record 6085973866; and, on `origin/main`, `ObjectQL#refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, `#readableIdsScopeOf`, `#hasObjectMiddleware`, `#resolveDatasourceBinding`, `#resolveEffectiveDatasource`, plugin-audit's `parent-record-read-gate.ts#planParentReads` and `#enumerateParentObjects`, `comment-access-hooks.ts` (its registrations and pointer columns), `objects/sys-comment.object.ts`, `core/src/security/readable-parent-ids.ts`, `security-plugin.ts#canReadObject`, `service-storage/src/index.ts`, and the rule texts (AGENTS.md's Prime Directives and Route and surface ownership, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md`, `execution-duties.md` and `landing-operations.md`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head, as read.** First read, 40 latest-per-name: 29 success, 6 skipped, Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of 6 in_progress, 0 failure. Second read (2026-10-16T01:03Z), 41 latest-per-name, all completed: 35 success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix row, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, Temporal Conformance), 0 failure. Success includes Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Test Core 1 to 6, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, the four Type Check jobs, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, and the two same-issue and same-path claim checks. No governed path in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface: one exported declaration widens, additively. Right as a change; its declaration is judged in ②.** `installAttachmentReadVisibility` is re-exported by `packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts` (line 112 on main), so its signature is the published face. Its first parameter widens from `AttachmentLifecycleEngine` to `AttachmentReadGateEngine`, an intersection whose added members (`registry.getAllObjects`, `hasObjectMiddleware`, `resolveEffectiveDatasource`) are all optional, and it gains an optional third parameter `getAdmission?: AttachmentReadAdmissionSource`. Every prior call still compiles and gets the whole-read probe; a three-argument call the base refused (TS2554, measured in the dev's A0 leg) is now accepted, and the entry's declaration reach grows by those two types. `installAttachmentAccessHooks`, `AttachmentSharingLike` and `AttachmentSecurityLike` are byte-identical. No REST route, no query parameter and no spec key moves. `StorageServicePlugin` is the one in-tree caller and passes a resolver that reads the `security` slot per read and answers `undefined` on an empty slot.

**The access floor, path by path. No path serves a `sys_attachment` row whose parent the caller may not read. Right.**

- *The leaf class.* `planAttachmentParentReads` enumerates every registry object whose name matches `OBJECT_NAME_RE`, except `sys_attachment`, and `computeParentVisibilityFilter` writes `{ parent_object: P, parent_id: { $in: ReadableIds.of(P) } }` for each leaf parent, ORed; `andIn` ANDs the result onto the caller's own `where`. The gate makes no engine call for a leaf. The engine composes each leaf at the executor boundary from `canReadObject(P, caller)` and `getReadFilter(P, caller)` (`readableIdsScopeOf`): a refusal, a throw, the deny sentinel, a non-filter answer or an unusable service each answer `$in: []`. `driver-sql` evaluates it as one subquery scoped by the driver's own tenant wall, which the probe's SYSTEM pre-scan never had. So a leaf serves at most the rows a direct read of P serves, except for D5.2's class, which the gate routes to the probe by the very function the engine refuses on.
- *D5.1, a delegated caller* (`isDelegatedCaller`, the engine's own `onBehalfOf.userId` test): the whole read is the probe, so every parent is read as the delegated caller through the middleware, where the delegator intersection applies. Main's path, unchanged.
- *D5.2, a parent an object-scoped read middleware narrows* (`hasObjectMiddleware`, the engine's own function): probed, with the pre-scan's `where` restricted to `parent_object $in` those parents (ANDed with the caller's `where`) and each candidate parent read as the caller. Main's path for those rows.
- *D5.3, a federated parent.* The gate compares `resolveEffectiveDatasource(P)` with `resolveEffectiveDatasource('sys_attachment')` where the engine compares `resolveDatasourceBinding().datasource`. Two `undefined`s (both via the default) compose on both; two equal explicit names compose on both; an explicit name against `undefined` is probed by the gate, and the engine would refuse it, except for a parent explicitly bound to the default driver's natural name, which the gate probes and the engine would compose. Stricter, never looser, so no parent the gate leafs is one the engine refuses on D5.3 (E5's record noted the same). On a telemetry-split deployment every parent on that datasource is probed, the limit D5.3 records.
- *No `canReadObject`, or no security service* (`hasObjectAdmission` answers false, a throwing `getService` included): the whole read is the probe, said once per engine. That is main's behaviour in that state. The guard's bound is the one E5's record named: it keys on the method's presence, not its SYSTEM answer; plugin-security's `canReadObject` admits `isSystem` by source, and this gate never composes under SYSTEM anyway, a system read being passed through before any filter.
- *A parent object the caller may not read.* Leaf: `canReadObject` false answers `$in: []`; nothing of P is read as the caller and no denial is logged (the integration suite pins `refusals` empty and no caller read of the doc or the vault). Probe: the caller-scoped read is refused by the security middleware and `resolveReadableParentIds` catches it into no visible id, as on main.
- *A dangling or parentless attachment.* A null or empty `parent_object` matches no branch; a null or empty `parent_id` is in no `$in`; a parent id that names no row is not in the subquery's answer. Pinned (`ids.dangling`, `ids.goneAttachment`). On the probe path `attachmentParentOf` skips the row, as on main.
- *A parent the registry does not hold.* The enumeration is the registry's, so no branch names it and the row is excluded; the engine's own `$in: []` for an unregistered leaf is never reached. On the probe path the caller-scoped read of it throws and is caught into no visible id. Pinned (`ids.unregistered`).
- *`sys_attachment` as a parent.* Excluded from the enumeration by name and skipped by `attachmentParentOf`, so a self-referencing row is excluded (pinned, `ids.selfRef`). This also keeps the consumer off a composition refusal: `sys_attachment` carries this very object-scoped middleware, so the engine would refuse a leaf over it.
- *"A probe that finds no candidate row is narrowed to no rows."* On the base, `computeParentVisibilityFilter` returned `null` for an empty pre-scan and the read ran unfiltered; the head returns `[]` branches, and a read left with no branch at all gets `READ_DENY_ALL`. The pre-scan is a SYSTEM superset of the caller's read, so an empty pre-scan means the caller's read matched nothing, and the only row this changes is one written between the pre-scan and the read, now hidden rather than served unjudged. Narrowing only; re-pinned in `attachment-read-visibility.test.ts`. On the leaf path no pre-scan runs, so the change applies to the two probe shapes alone, and a restricted probe with no candidates leaves the leaves in place and serves nothing of the probed parents.
- *The `controlled_by_parent` master route (`ce3d0ad419`).* That route is `installAttachmentAccessHooks#mayEditParent` through `checkControlledByParentWrite`, the write gate, and the diff's hunks do not touch it. On the read side the derivation for a `controlled_by_parent` parent is `getReadFilter`'s (ADR-0055 §2's mechanism (b), which ADR-0139's Context names as part of `getReadFilter`): the leaf carries it inside its subquery and the probe applies it through the middleware, the same filter by `getReadFilter`'s own contract.

**D3. Right.** The middleware body is `andIn(ctx, await computeParentVisibilityFilter(...)); return next()` with no catch. The one remaining catch is around `probeBranches` alone: a fault of the probe's SYSTEM pre-scan or of its caller-scoped parent reads answers `READ_DENY_ALL` and is said. Neither of those reads carries a leaf of this gate, so the catch cannot meet this read's composition refusal, and a refusal raised by `next()` propagates with the leaves still in the WHERE (unit pin) and reaches the caller as `{ code: INTERNAL_ERROR, status: 500 }` naming the driver (integration pin on a refusing driver, `find` and `count`). The envelope is the engine's `readableIdsRefusalError` or the driver's `refuseReadableIdsOnce`, E2's and E4's, not this diff's; under ADR-0112's 5xx amendment a declared server fault keeps its message, as E5's record read it. One observation, not this diff's: a probed parent that is itself a leaf-emitting gated object (an attachment on a `sys_activity` row) is read as the caller through `resolveReadableParentIds`, whose own catch answers no visible id to any failure of that nested read, a refusing driver's included. That is core's fail-closed rule on main and it narrows; on such a driver the outer read fails 500 on its own leaves regardless.

**The three D5 copies agree, and the one disagreement is stricter.** `planAttachmentParentReads` mirrors `planParentReads` function for function: the same delegated test, the same `hasObjectMiddleware` call, the same `resolveEffectiveDatasource` comparison against the gated object, the same whole-read states, the same name order. They differ only in enumeration, rightly: the audit gate excludes `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` and admits `namedParents` because those are the audit writer's objects, while an attachment may hang off any registered object, so this gate excludes only itself, as its probe did on main. Against the engine: D5.1 and D5.2 are the same tests; D5.3 differs only in the default-driver-natural-name case, where both consumers probe and the engine would compose. No disagreement is a widening, and no composition refusal can reach the consumer from a mis-classified parent.

**Served-set changes, each named. Right.** (a) A broad read is served every attachment whose parent the caller may read, with a true `total`, on any table size (measured: member 1,755 to 2,302 of 2,302; administrator 1,998 to 2,604; dogfood member 64 to 80 of 80). A widening within the caller's read; the window was the defect. (b) The empty-probe narrowing above. (c) On `driver-mongodb` a `sys_attachment` read fails `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500: ADR-0139 D3 and Consequences, O3, #22788 note 3; the changeset names it. (d) A broad read now runs the restricted probe's SYSTEM pre-scan for the middleware-gated parents on every read even when none holds an attachment (dogfood: 8 parents, 0 rows): a bounded cost, not a wrong answer.

**Pins read against the diff.** `attachment-read-leaf.integration.test.ts` (real `ObjectQL` and `SqlDriver`, 10 cases): both members served exactly their readable set past the window with `count` equal; the administrator's page of 20 over a true total; the vault, deleted-parent, dangling, unregistered, self-referencing and other-member gated rows hidden; no refusal and no caller read of a leaf parent; one leaf per enumerated parent with the gated and federated parents probed beside them; the delegated whole-read probe bounded and never wider than the truth; the O2 reading; the refusing driver's envelope on `find` and `count`. `attachment-read-leaf.test.ts` (stand-in engine, 20 cases): branch per parent and no read for a leaf; each D5 class with the restricted pre-scan's `where`, `limit` and SYSTEM context; the four security-source states and the three engine gaps, said once each; a restricted probe failure denying all; the cap warning naming its class; `next()`'s refusal propagating with the leaves kept. `attachment-read-visibility.test.ts`: the one re-pin. The dogfood scan-cap suite is rewritten for the other side of the bound with its control kept (a 2,000-row window would leave a visible row outside), the hidden row and the ghost parents still excluded, and the owner served the hidden row. Each ablation A0 to A7 is named with its red count in the PR body; the check-runs on the head are the verdict on them.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23732-attachment-readable-ids.md`: `@objectstack/service-storage` `minor`. The level is right. A consumer observes more rows served within access and a true `total` (a fix), a new failure mode on a refusing driver that E3, E4 and E5 already shipped at `minor` as the ruled consequence, and an additive optional parameter on an exported installer, which takes at least `minor` under the WHICH LEVEL ruling (the changeset gate's own header, and PR #22513's record). Sentence by sentence the changeset body matches the diff: the leaf's shape and exclusions, the three probed classes with the gated examples (`sys_comment`, `sys_comment_reaction`, `sys_activity` and `sys_audit_log` each carry an object-scoped registration on main), the no-`canReadObject` state, the empty-probe narrowing, the mongodb 500, and the installer sentence.
- **The `Clause-②: no` line, in the changeset body and in the PR body, is wrong: `yes` is owed.** The criterion the line answers is the protocol's (`clause2-line.mjs` cites it, `execution-duties.md` spells it): does the card relax an accept set or expand the public face, where the public face is what the package's built entry declaration reaches, the re-exported names plus every type reachable through their props, parameters and return types. `installAttachmentReadVisibility` is re-exported; its accept set is relaxed (a third argument the base refused is accepted) and its reach grows by `AttachmentReadGateEngine` and `AttachmentReadAdmissionSource`. Both limbs say `yes`. The precedent the dev cites does not carry. PR #22513 was declared `no (narrowing)`, and its contract record 6085973866 says of the same act in the same package that the diff "also adds two exported types and an optional parameter to two published indexes; that additive act takes at least `minor` under the WHICH LEVEL ruling", and that the record "is the contract-tier review a widening declaration would have owed". That is a widening passed under a `(narrowing)` arm that already owed the tier, not a ruling that an optional parameter is `no`. E5's `no` rested on its installers not being re-exported (its body and record 6196593905 both say so); here the installer is. The repo's other reading agrees: a new optional member on a published contract "IS Clause-② `yes`" by the mechanical floor (`docs/audits/2026-09-loadmany-consumer-census.md` §5). Under `landing-operations.md` an incorrect `no` is an auditable false declaration, so this record cannot pass the head as written. The remedy is one line in two places and no code: the changeset body's line and the PR body's line read `Clause-②: yes`; the level stays `minor`, which `check-changeset-no-major` accepts for a `yes`; the claim comment 6204165226's line is the dispatching seat's to amend. Every judgment in ① and ③ holds for that head, whose diff against `main` is unchanged in code.
- ADR-0087: no marker is owed; nothing authorable, stored or published is removed, renamed or narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (the comment-thread gate has no pointer pair): not this PR's to decide, and honestly left.** `sys-comment.object.ts` on main declares `thread_id` as one text field spelled `{object}:{record_id}` and no `parent_object`, `object_name` or `record_id` field; `comment-access-hooks.ts` parses it (`parseCommentThreadId`) and ANDs `{ thread_id: { $in } }`. D1's leaf stands for P's `id` values at a `$in` comparand, so no branch of D4's shape exists over `thread_id`. The PR body says exactly this, changes nothing in `plugin-audit`, and carries `Part of #23732`, which the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check reads green. The decision is the card owner's and the maintainer's; this record adds nothing to it.
- **Q2 (the reaction gate's one parent is on D5.2's list): not this PR's to decide, and honestly left.** ADR-0139 D5.2 names `sys_comment` by name; `comment-access-hooks.ts` registers its read gate with `{ object: 'sys_comment' }` (line 880 on main) and the reaction branch keys on `comment_id`, so `hasObjectMiddleware('sys_comment')` is true and the engine would refuse a leaf over it. The PR's text on D5.2 matches the ADR's, and the plan row's reaction pin against D5's text is the owner's call, as E5's activity pins were. No reaction gate code is touched.
- **Q3 (the optional third parameter): answered in ②. The declaration must read `yes`; the level stays `minor`.** The precedent cited is read there and does not carry.
- **`Part of`, the claim checks:** right. The PR names both undecided gates, touches neither, and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` and `No other open PR may claim the same issue` are green.
- **Out-of-scope finding (the D5 classification now exists twice beside the engine's):** carrier #22788, the engine lane, agreed; the two copies are read against each other and the engine in ①, and one helper in `@objectstack/core` beside `resolveReadableParentIds` would make them one.
- **Acceptance note, the QA checklist item `attachments-storage.read-inherits-parent-rls`:** its `knownGaps` and `automated.ref` describe clause 3's 2,000-row fail-closed cap for a broad read, which a broad read over an ordinary parent no longer meets; the rewritten pin keeps the `@proof` tag. The PR says "Carrier: none". A ledger sentence describing a limit the runtime no longer has needs an owner: the seat names #23732 itself as the carrier (it stays open for the two other gates and closes on E7's last switch), or files the one-line edit. Not a defect of this diff.
- **The restricted probe's per-read SYSTEM pre-scan for parents that hold no attachment:** a bounded cost the PR names; no action owed here.
- **Interim letter C:** never landed on this gate (ruling W, as E5 found), so nothing was retired. Right.
- **The dev's seven deviations** (the `Part of` keyword; the bare `--` trap on the package test; one joined lock call; a refused `--replacement ""` attempt; scratch suites absent from every commit; the gate list re-derived; the model-free trailer pair): none touches the diff's contract or its pins.
